verdict.rationale: Undermind's docs describe a deep literature review that starts from an open-ended research goal, plans its own searches, follows citations and key authors, and stops only when new searches stop finding relevant papers. It then produces a ranked list with a written synthesis, and the product asks clarifying follow-up questions first. Hands-on reports corroborate this multi-step behavior: 3-6 minute searches, good follow-up questions, a 'Discovery Progress and Exhaustiveness' readout, and comprehensive topic coverage. Missing for 10: documentation exposing the intermediate investigation steps to the user, and consistent depth on niche or gray-literature queries (one user saw a refined search return nearly the same results; another saw much gray literature missed).
